run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Route `Field.Control`'s controlled `value` prop through the same `useValueChanged` layout-effect sync path its sibling controls (Switch, Checkbox, Select, Number Field, OTP Field, Combobox) already use, instead of driving dirty/filled/validation only from the DOM `change` event. This fixes dirty state that never cleared for non-string controlled values and field state (filled/dirty/validity) that went stale after a programmatic value change.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the four correctness claims in the supplied PR-body spec (serialize the controlled value before the dirty comparison; sync filled/dirty/validation on programmatic changes; respect `details.cancel()`; let a rejected/rewritten controlled value never reach field state) are all implemented and each is covered by a new test that passes at head. The PR's own jsdom render-count benchmark table is a supporting performance assertion this review could not reproduce with the PR's exact harness; a repository test asserting the same one-render-per-keystroke property passes, which is consistent but not identical evidence.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (2 files, `FieldControl.tsx` and `FieldControl.test.tsx`). Read every `useValueChanged` call site (Switch, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group, Select, Number Field input, OTP Field, Combobox) and the shared `useFieldValidation`/`useRegisterFieldControl`/`useFieldControlRegistration` helpers to confirm the new call site matches existing architecture and does not race the async-validation commit-id guard. Focused test run once at head: `TZ=UTC VITEST_ENV=jsdom ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project @base-ui/react packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.test.tsx` — 26 passed, 1 skipped (SSR-only, correctly `skipIf(isJSDOM)`). One concurrency safety premise (a stale in-flight async validator for a superseded controlled value cannot publish over the newer value) was verified `holds` by a fresh-context worker.

observations.fact: `NumberFieldInput`'s `useValueChanged` callback only clears errors and revalidates; unlike `FieldControl`'s combined callback it does not also call `setDirty`/`setFilled`, because `NumberFieldRoot`'s `setValue` already applies those for both controlled and uncontrolled paths.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"With value={5}, the baseline was the number 5, so \"5\" !== 5 held forever"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:86 serializes the controlled value (`String(value)`) before it is registered (FieldControl.tsx:90-97) and compared for dirtiness (FieldControl.tsx:111); FieldControl.test.tsx:116-140 (`clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value`) passes at head (vitest run, 26/27 passed, 1 skipped).

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"Programmatic changes left the field stale ... filled, dirty, or validity"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-115 runs `clearErrors`/`setDirty`/`setFilled`/`validation.change` from a `useValueChanged` layout effect keyed on the controlled value, so any external change to `value` — not just a DOM `change` event — re-syncs field state; FieldControl.test.tsx:142-167 (`syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically`) passes.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling. It was ignored."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:153 adds `!details.isCanceled` to the guard before `clearErrors`/`validation.change`; FieldControl.test.tsx:189-201 (`does not validate when the change is canceled`) passes.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:140-146: `onChange` always calls `onValueChange` but returns immediately after for a controlled field, before touching dirty/filled/validation; the same value-prop-owns-controlled-path shape is used in NumberFieldInput.tsx:89-110, OTPFieldRoot.tsx:199, AriaCombobox.tsx:1055-1070, and SelectRoot.tsx:243.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/performance table ("Renders per keystroke ... This PR ... Number Field")
requirements.evidence: The PR's jsdom render-count benchmark harness is not part of this diff and could not be re-run here. FieldControl.test.tsx:47-80 (`renders once per keystroke for controlled input changes`) is a repository test with the same intent and passes, which is consistent with the claim but is not the cited benchmark; nothing in this review's decision depends on the exact benchmark numbers, since the correctness findings above are independently verified through code and tests.

tasks.premise: When a controlled Field.Control's serialized value changes while a previous validation.change()/commit() call for an earlier value still has its async validate() promise pending, the new layout-effect-driven call to validation.change(serializedValue) synchronously increments validationCommitIdRef.current before the earlier commit() call's pending await resolves, so the post-await guard discards the stale result and it never overwrites the field's validity state for the newer value.
